comment: Differences between the FFmpeg 8.1.3 baseline and the current shim that are explained and accepted (AC-7). Every other difference must fail the harness. Kept next to the baseline so the comparison is reproducible. The 2026-11-25 follow-up re-ran the harness after fixing F-06, F-07 and F-08: those fixes intentionally change the decoded samples where the old shim was wrong, so the affected fields legitimately differ from the 8.1.3 baseline.

allowed.reason: F-06 fix: the shim no longer re-seeks for every mixer block, so the 4096+1 block pattern now equals one continuous read (proven bit-exact in tests/audio_blocks.rs). The 8.1.3 baseline recorded the corrupt per-block output; the difference is the fix, not a regression.

F-07 fix: the first read from position 0 no longer seeks, so the AAC decoder is not flushed before the first frame. The new stream equals the bundled ffmpeg CLI's decode of the same file (checked sample by sample); the baseline recorded the post-seek stream.
F-06 fix: same mechanism as audio_aac_sine.m4a; the block pattern is now bit-identical to the continuous read (tests/audio_blocks.rs).
F-07 fix: same mechanism as audio_aac_sine.m4a; the long read now starts without a seek.
F-06 fix: the mixer's overlapping block pattern is served from the history buffer instead of re-seeking, so it equals the continuous read; the baseline recorded the per-block re-seek.
F-06 fix: resampled 44.1 kHz source; the block pattern no longer resets the resampler and is bit-identical to the continuous read.
F-06 fix: MDCT decoder pre-roll is decoded and discarded on a seek, and the block pattern no longer seeks at all; the result equals the continuous read.
F-06 fix: the block pattern is served from the history buffer and equals the continuous read.
F-06 fix: same as audio_opus.ogg; this entry is also the F-07 alignment case (1 ms timestamps) and is bit-identical to the Ogg remux in tests/audio_anchor.rs.
F-06 fix: the block pattern no longer re-seeks into the stereo/mono parameter change, so it equals the continuous read.

F-08 fix: this is the unindexed MPEG-TS fixture with a 483 ms start offset. The old shim returned the next I-frame for every request from frame 15 on (audit experiment G: all 88 frames wrong); the new output is the requested frame for every index, so the hash necessarily differs from the 8.1.3 baseline.
F-08 fix: same fixture; random access now decodes across the target instead of returning a later frame.
